setup: The Qheadache game is installed on a personal computer and no network connection or external services are required to launch it.
action: The player starts Qheadache from the desktop or application launcher.
expected_observation: The game opens and presents itself as a self-contained standalone puzzle game, ready to be played locally without requiring sign-in, online access, or other companion software.

setup: A first-time child player and an experienced adult player each have access to the same Qheadache installation.
action: Each player opens the game and begins a new puzzle session.
expected_observation: The game presents a consistent, approachable puzzle interface that is usable by both beginners and adults, without age-restricted content or controls that block either player group from starting play.

setup: Qheadache is running and a puzzle is ready to be started.
action: The player begins a puzzle session.
expected_observation: A graphical board is displayed with visible grid or play-area boundaries and movable blocks rendered on the board for interaction.

setup: A puzzle challenge is in progress on the graphical board and at least one block has an adjacent open space in a legal move direction.
action: The player moves a block into the empty space to rearrange the board toward the target arrangement.
expected_observation: The selected block changes position on the board, the empty space shifts accordingly, and the board state updates to reflect the new puzzle configuration.

setup: The game is open in a normal, everyday play session with default puzzle settings and no error conditions present.
action: The player starts a standard puzzle and makes a sequence of valid block moves.
expected_observation: The game accepts the moves smoothly, updates the board normally, and continues play without crashes, freezes, or other interruptions.

setup: The player has completed part of a puzzle session and the game is configured to preserve session results.
action: The player ends the session or saves progress after making several moves and spending time on the puzzle.
expected_observation: The game records the session's progress and results, including elapsed time, number of actions taken, and any score achieved, so the information is available after the session ends.

setup: A new player opens Qheadache for the first time without prior tutorial knowledge.
action: The player begins the first puzzle and attempts to make a valid move using the on-screen controls or direct block interaction.
expected_observation: The player can understand how to start and play the puzzle with minimal guidance, using clear controls and immediately understandable board behavior.

setup: An adult player who has completed several puzzles before opens Qheadache for a new session.
action: The player starts a fresh puzzle after having already experienced prior challenges.
expected_observation: The game presents enough puzzle challenge, variation, or replay appeal to remain engaging for an adult player rather than feeling trivial or repetitive.

setup: A puzzle is active and the board contains both legal and illegal move opportunities.
action: The player attempts to solve the puzzle by moving blocks in sequence until the target arrangement is reached.
expected_observation: The game clearly indicates which moves are allowed, prevents illegal moves, and allows the player to complete the puzzle without ambiguous board behavior or confusing feedback.

setup: The player has already made several moves in the current puzzle and has not yet solved it.
action: The player views the in-game status display while continuing to play.
expected_observation: The game shows understandable progress information such as current state, move count, elapsed time, or completion progress so the player can clearly tell how far they have advanced.

setup: The player has completed a puzzle once and the session results have been recorded.
action: The player starts the same puzzle again or chooses a replay option to attempt a better result.
expected_observation: The game allows the puzzle to be replayed and supports a new attempt with the opportunity to improve prior time, move count, or score.

setup: The player has Qheadache available on their device and has previously played at least one session.
action: The player returns to the game on a later occasion and starts another puzzle session.
expected_observation: The game remains a self-contained, enjoyable standalone title that supports repeated return play without requiring external dependencies or a separate companion platform.

setup: A person is using Qheadache as the active puzzle player.
action: The player launches the game, plays a puzzle, and reviews the results at the end of the session.
expected_observation: The game provides the player with a usable puzzle experience, making player interaction and satisfaction central to the session flow.

setup: A game designer or content owner reviews the puzzle content and challenge behavior in Qheadache.
action: The designer or content owner inspects the available puzzle setup and result presentation during gameplay.
expected_observation: The puzzle content, challenge structure, and outcome reporting can be evaluated and tuned from a content perspective, supporting design ownership of the gameplay experience.

setup: An administrative or support role is available for Qheadache in an environment where operational assistance may be needed.
action: The administrator or support person accesses the game's available support-related information or operational context.
expected_observation: Where such a role exists, the game can be supported in a way that allows assistance with issues such as player progress or game usage, without affecting normal player play.

setup: The administrator is signed in to Qheadache with permission to manage puzzle content, and the puzzle catalog is currently showing the active set of available puzzles.
action: The administrator adds a new puzzle to the catalog and disables one existing puzzle so it will no longer be offered to players.
expected_observation: The puzzle management screen reflects the updated catalog, the new puzzle appears as available, the disabled puzzle is marked unavailable, and players will only see the currently enabled puzzles in the game.

setup: The administrator is signed in to Qheadache with access to the board configuration tools, and the current board layout is the default grid used by players.
action: The administrator changes the board layout from the default arrangement to a larger grid with a different number of rows and columns.
expected_observation: The board layout editor shows the new grid dimensions, the saved configuration is displayed as the active board layout, and future games use the updated layout.

setup: The administrator is signed in to Qheadache and is editing a predefined challenge template that is available to players.
action: The administrator updates the challenge by changing the puzzle start state and the target solution condition, then saves the challenge.
expected_observation: The challenge details are stored with the new starting arrangement and win condition, and the updated predefined challenge is the one presented to players when selected.

setup: The administrator is signed in to Qheadache and is viewing the difficulty settings for the current game configuration.
action: The administrator increases the challenge difficulty by reducing the allowed moves and enabling a stricter time limit.
expected_observation: The difficulty settings screen shows the new limits, the saved difficulty profile is active, and players receive the updated move and time constraints in subsequent games.

setup: The administrator is signed in to Qheadache and is managing challenge assignments for player skill levels.
action: The administrator assigns an easy challenge set to beginners and a separate advanced challenge set to experienced players, then saves the assignment rules.
expected_observation: The assignment rules show beginner-only challenges and advanced-only challenges mapped to the correct player groups, and beginners and advanced players are offered different challenge lists when they start a game.

setup: The administrator is signed in to Qheadache and the results dashboard contains saved player progress records from previous games.
action: The administrator opens the player results and progress records view and selects a specific player to review.
expected_observation: The administrator can see the selected player's completed challenges, completion times, and progress history on the results dashboard.

setup: The administrator is signed in to Qheadache and player results and progress records are currently stored in the system.
action: The administrator chooses to clear all stored results and confirms the clearing action.
expected_observation: The system removes the stored player results and progress records, the records list becomes empty or reset, and no cleared records remain visible to the administrator.

setup: The administrator is signed in to Qheadache and player results and progress records are available for archiving.
action: The administrator selects a set of results and progress records and archives them.
expected_observation: The selected records are moved out of the active results view into an archived state, the archived records are no longer shown in the main results list, and the administrator can confirm they were preserved in the archive.

setup: The administrator is signed in to Qheadache from one administrative session, and the game is being used by players through the centralized service.
action: The administrator saves a configuration change to a puzzle, board layout, or challenge setting from the administration interface.
expected_observation: The saved change becomes the active centralized configuration for Qheadache, so the updated setting is reflected consistently wherever the game is accessed rather than remaining local to one session or device.

setup: The administrator is signed in to Qheadache and prepares to change a game setting that is not a very small immediate-safe update, such as a challenge rule or board configuration.
action: The administrator saves the non-small configuration change while a game session is already in progress.
expected_observation: The current running game continues with the existing settings, and the change takes effect only the next time the game starts, rather than being applied immediately to the active session.

setup: The Qheadache role model is under review, and only the administrator role is currently confirmed in the system design documentation.
action: A reviewer attempts to determine whether a separate technical support role is available for managing Qheadache support tasks.
expected_observation: The system requirements do not confirm a separate technical support role, leaving the role definition unresolved and requiring a follow-up decision before that access path can be accepted.
